question: Can nanoRSI, driven by GLM-5.3 (full tier, not flash), produce clear frozen-tested improvements on complete evaluation tasks reported by upstream papers and repositories?

final_panel.note: test split uses a denser 321-point grid containing inputs absent from the 161-point selection grid

tasks.mode: population search (size 4, generations 2, workers 2, crossover enabled), count-only feedback preserved

search_outcomes.winner: first-generation direct candidate (crossover occurred in the population but did not produce the winner — reported honestly)

audit: both workspaces: zero expected-answer leakage, zero silent bypass, verify passes
limits: Single runs, single seed, one model tier; the sine test split shares the task family's grid formula (denser, not disjoint); k-module has a deterministic hidden target so test re-measures selection; upstream author-reported results are not reproduced — these are independent nanoRSI runs of their tasks. Combined with the earlier GLM-5.3-Flash function-minimization study (0.9418 -> 0.9960), three upstream tasks have now been run end to end on this platform.
